title: Pixels to Tokens: Token Space Efficient Active Learning for Low-Budget Semantic Segmentation
gist: TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), a NeurIPS paper with University of Waterloo authors, is presented as the first pixel-level active learning framework built on ViT token representations: it selects pixels to label on a frozen ViT's native token lattice and beats prior baselines by up to +24.36 mIoU with one labeled pixel per image, reaching up to 97% of fully supervised segmentation performance with 10 labeled pixels.

insights.claim: Current active learning strategies for vision-transformer and foundation-model backbones mostly select at the patch or region level, which keeps annotation requirements high because extensive pixel labeling is still needed for semantic segmentation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Labeling cost, not model capacity, is the binding constraint for segmentation; methods that cut pixel labels shrink the data-annotation spend.
insights.quote: current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling
insights.locator: While foundation models and vision transformers

insights.claim: Pixel-level active learning with ViTs in a low-budget regime is hard because with as little as one pixel query per image a method must both find the most informative locations and train a reliable decoder head from an extremely sparse signal.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Frames the technical bar any low-label segmentation product must clear.
insights.locator: Extending ViT-based AL to the pixel-level

insights.claim: TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning) keeps the ViT backbone frozen and runs diversity-based pixel selection directly on the ViT's native token lattice, avoiding artifacts from interpolating token embeddings up to dense pixel resolution.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Working in token space rather than upsampled pixel space suggests cheaper selection on frozen foundation models, with no backbone fine-tuning.
insights.quote: avoiding the artifacts introduced by interpolating token embeddings to dense pixel resolutions

insights.claim: TEAL uses a two-level MaxHerding strategy over multi-layer token descriptors to choose representative candidates, then refines them with margin-based uncertainty on a finer decoder grid.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A diversity-then-uncertainty pipeline is a reusable recipe for label-efficient vision training.
insights.locator: Our framework applies a two-level MaxHerding

insights.claim: On CamVid, Cityscapes, ADE20K and Pascal Context, TEAL improves on the strongest prior active learning baseline by up to +24.36 mIoU when only one pixel per image is labeled.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Large gains at the lowest budget point to a big drop in annotation cost for segmentation in domains like autonomous driving scenes.
insights.quote: improving over the strongest baseline by up to +24.36mIoU with a single labeled pixel (px) per image

insights.claim: TEAL reaches up to 97% of fully supervised semantic segmentation performance with just 10 labeled pixels per image.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Near-supervised accuracy from 10 pixels per image weakens the case for dense pixel annotation spend.
insights.quote: reaching up to 97% of fully supervised performance with just 10 px

insights.claim: TEAL's gains persist even when every baseline uses the same DINOv3 backbone, so the improvement comes from combining token-space selection with decoder-grid uncertainty refinement, not from a stronger backbone.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Shows the method gives an edge independent of the backbone, so it can sit on top of whichever foundation model is current.
insights.quote: the improvements persist when all baselines are equipped with the same DINOv3 backbone
insights.locator: To rigorously establish the source of the gains
